title: Huh.
description:
## What.
Now, you may have noticed that that syntax looks like a blobfish having a seziure. That is correct. Haskell is something called a _Functional Programming Language_, which basically means that you describe what you want to happen instead of how it should happen. First, before we get into haskell monstrousitys, let's cover the boilerplate.
Haskell programs start in main:
```haskell
main :: IO ()
```
This basically means "Main is a function that does nothing meaningfull to the program and can modify the system with Input and Output", to break this down: `main`: this is called main. `::`: says from now on on this line is what the function is for. `IO`: This function will modify things, such as taking input and output. `()`: This function returns nothing meaningfull.
Now, actually printing to console. To actually code in a function, there are two ways: For single line, you can just do this:
```haskell
main = <code>
```
However, if you have multiple lines, you must do
```haskell
main = do
    <code>
```
and the function ends when you un-indent. To print a string you use `putStrLn "text here"`.
You may be seeing all this function talk. Don't worry, their comming soon.

## Assignment:
Somebody deleted out main function! Recreate it. It should welcome our users to their new phone. Make it print 2 lines, `Welcome to your new pPhone 18!`, and `Bonus screen protectors available for 299.99`.
